text:
incident-bot: PAGER: elevated 5xx + tail latency observed for hosted inference endpoints in az1a. affected backends: inference-prod-az1a. auto-alert threshold breached (5m error rate > 8%). paging ash_oncall :rotating_light:

ash_oncall: on it. looking at graphs now. assigning priority P1 until we know customer impact.

miguel_r: I see a burst of ENI rx drops and retransmits starting ~23:02 UTC, coincident with resolver timeouts to our VPC resolver (10.0.2.5). per-host kernel netstat shows queue_full stats.

nia_ops: same — kube-proxy logs show connection reset to metadata/resolver around the same window. DNS latency spikes from ~1ms to 450ms for >80% of calls.

ash_oncall: can we confirm if this is local host NIC saturation vs upstream resolver? any packet capture?

miguel_r: running tcpdump now on a sample node. short snippet: ```
# tcpdump -ni eth0 udp port 53
23:02:14.123 IP 10.0.1.45.34567 > 10.0.2.5.53: 1234+ A? resolver.example
23:02:14.574 IP 10.0.2.5.53 > 10.0.1.45.34567: 1234 ServFail
23:02:15.001 IP 10.0.1.45.34567 > 10.0.2.5.53: 1235+ A? resolver.example
```

ash_oncall: ok so resolver is returning SERVFAILs + slow responses. that will blow up our connection pool and increase token latency.

infra-bot: NOTE: az1a host NIC metrics showing tx/rx packet drops > 30% for the last 6m on g5 instances in inference-prod-az1a. recommend traffic steering to az1b/az1c.

ash_oncall: miguel, can you open a route-shift and start redirecting new inference traffic to az1b? prefer automated runtime routing but doing manual to be safe. command below.

miguel_r: running: ```
rwctl routing shift --service inference-prod --from az1a --to az1b --mode gradual --duration 10m --reason "az1a resolver/backoff" 
```

pagerduty: ash_oncall acknowledged pager at 23:04 UTC. escalation to SRE lead if not resolved by 23:20 UTC.

ash_oncall: doing a canary first (5% -> 20%). watching request latencies/errors.

(5m later)
miguel_r: canary looks good. error rate in az1b is normal, az1a errors continue. increasing shift to 60%.

cs_priya: which customers are impacted? I see 2 enterprise tenants with elevated errors in their dashboards. starting outreach: short email + status page update.

nia_ops: also starting node drains in az1a for the worst hosts (ids: i-0a11, i-0a22). will cordon+drain to avoid new allocations there.

ash_oncall: good. doing KV cache warmup on az1b instances after the traffic shift to avoid cold-start regressions.

infra-bot: TRAFFIC SHIFT COMPLETE: 100% new traffic routed away from az1a at 23:14 UTC. legacy sticky sessions still draining.

miguel_r: monitoring shows overall system latency back to baseline after shift. some requests that hit az1a still 502; drain should clear.

ash_oncall: raising an ops ticket with AWS support: reported behaviour looks like ENI offload regression or local host driver hit causing resolver timeouts. attaching logs and tcpdump.

(aws-support-bot posts)
aws-support-bot: Case #123456789 opened with AWS. preliminary note: "We observe high RX drops at hypervisor/host link layer; investigating instance-level NIC offload"

cs_priya: sent customer comms: short note on degraded infra in az1a, mitigation in place, full update to follow. customers asked for ETA — giving 2hr initial window.

ash_oncall: capture timeline for postmortem: 23:02 start, 23:04 pager, 23:14 traffic fully rerouted, 23:20 drains finishing. severity P1 -> mitigated.

miguel_r: follow-ups: (1) collect kernel dmesg and ethtool stats from affected hosts (2) validate route table & resolver HA config (3) ensure runtime routing has faster automatic fallback thresholds. I'll own (1) and (3).

nia_ops: I'll own (2) and coordinate with networking team to verify resolver scaling/HA and consider fallback to third-party resolver if needed.

ash_oncall: thanks. assigning follow-up owners, adding to postmortem board. closing pager thread; moving to post-incident channel for RCA. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: RESOLVED: pager cleared at 23:22 UTC. severity downgraded to P2 for RCA work.

ash_oncall: final note for thread: customer impact limited thanks to rapid routing shift; we'll run a simulated resolver failure test in staging to validate the fallback. owners: miguel_r, nia_ops. cs_priya will finalize customer follow-up.

cs_priya: will publish status page update in 1h after RCA draft.

(END)
